title: Tamil Nadu Investment Panel Sets $72 Billion Export Target at First Meeting
excerpt: The Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission, chaired by Chief Secretary Sai Kumar, reviewed 112 MoUs worth ₹1.14 lakh crore and fast-tracked work on a New Industrial Policy for 2027.
body:
• Tamil Nadu's new Investment Promotion Commission held its first meeting on Friday, chaired by Chief Secretary Sai Kumar, and set a target of raising the state's exports from $59 billion to $72 billion.
  • The panel reviewed 112 investment MoUs worth ₹1.14 lakh crore signed since May 2026, with a potential 1,32,771 jobs; 83 have progressed to the land-allotment stage or beyond.
  • The commission will fast-track major proposals of ₹200 crore and above, projects promising at least 5,000 jobs, and proposals stuck between departments.
  • For businesses, the state's Single Window Portal has disposed of 19,323 of 21,753 applications received, and preparatory work on a New Industrial Policy 2027 is being expedited.

Tamil Nadu's newly formed Investment Promotion Commission held its first meeting in Chennai on Friday, setting a target of lifting the state's exports from $59 billion to $72 billion as part of a longer-term goal of building a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036, according to Business Standard and the state Industries Department's statement on the meeting.

The Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission (TNIPC) was constituted on November 3, 2026, under Section 16-A of the Tamil Nadu Business Facilitation Act, 2018, as amended through the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion and Facilitation Legislation, 2026. It is chaired by the Chief Secretary, with the Additional Chief Secretary for Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce as member-secretary and convener. Its 20 members are drawn from departments including Finance, Energy, Information Technology, Housing and Urban Development, Transport, Environment, Labour Welfare and Commercial Taxes, and representatives of the Madras Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the Confederation of Indian Industry and the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry took part in the first meeting.

What the panel will fast-track

The commission's remit covers major investment proposals of ₹200 crore and above, projects expected to generate at least 5,000 jobs, and proposals that need coordination across departments. It will also work on helping Tamil Nadu industry use the opportunities opened up by India's free trade agreements. The Industries Department said discussions covered the proposed new industrial policy, single-window clearances, the progress of investment MoUs signed since the government led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay came to power in May 2026, and measures to boost the state's exports.

MoUs: ₹1.14 lakh crore on the table

Since May 2026, the state has signed 112 MoUs worth ₹1.14 lakh crore, with potential employment for 1,32,771 people. Of those, 83 MoUs have progressed to the land-allotment stage and beyond, and the government put overall MoU implementation progress at 74.11%. At the meeting, the Chief Secretary also inaugurated a remote approval system for the Industries Department covering 37 industrial services, 18 of which have already been operationalised.

New Industrial Policy 2027

The meeting reviewed preparatory work for the New Industrial Policy 2027. "Consultations with various stakeholders have been undertaken since July 2026. The existing industrial policies are also being evaluated to identify areas requiring revision and improvement. Directions have been issued to expedite the preparation of the new policy," the Industries Department said in its statement. The panel also reviewed more than 25 reforms carried out across 11 departments through 23 government orders since May 2026, including simplifying land-use conversion for industry and removing certain no-objection-certificate requirements from the Agriculture Department and district Collectors.

What it means for businesses

For companies dealing with the state, the operational numbers are in the single-window system: 21,753 applications have been received on the Single Window Portal and 19,323 disposed of. Investment-related clearances worth ₹1,700 crore have been facilitated, and additional proposals exceeding ₹2,000 crore have been converted into actionable proposals over the past six months. The export target — from $59 billion to $72 billion — was reported without a specific deadline in the government's statement, and sits inside the state's stated ambition of a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036.

What's next

The next markers are the draft of the New Industrial Policy 2027, which the Industries Department has been directed to expedite, and whether the 74.11% MoU implementation rate keeps rising as the 83 projects that have cleared land allotment move toward construction. The commission's focus on proposals of ₹200 crore and above means the largest projects will get a single coordination point rather than moving department by department.
